title: Finite compact supports have a uniform Tor bound after dense refinement
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $F_n=Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}=Rp_{0*,n}j_{0!}$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

Let $d\geq0$ satisfy $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-dimension]. The dense refinement $c=\mathsf{Dense}(c_0)=(j,p)$ of [def-nagata-dense-refinement] is a compactification of $f$ whose ambient scheme $\overline X=\operatorname{SIm}(j_0)$ is finite type over $k$, whose open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ is topologically dense, and whose dimension satisfies $\dim\overline X=\dim X\leq d$.

For every $n\geq1$, integers $a\leq b$, and intrinsically bounded constructible $L\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the object $Rp_{*,n}j_!L$ is intrinsically bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$. The canonical compactification comparison identifies it with $F_nL$, and $F_nL$ has the same constructibility and Tor interval. The compactification $c_0$ is arbitrary and the interval is independent of $n$ and of the choice of $c_0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: "replace the compactifying scheme by the scheme-theoretic closure of X" through the finite compact-support site comparison; old Steps 3–5.

proof.text: First check the hypothesis for the scheme-image construction. The map $f=p_0j_0$ is quasi-compact since it is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The map $p_0$ is proper, hence separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and therefore quasi-separated: its diagonal is a closed immersion, whose inverse image of an affine open is a closed affine subscheme and hence quasi-compact [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to $X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{p_0}Y$. It gives quasi-compactness of the open immersion $j_0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: hypotheses for replacing the compactifying scheme by the scheme-theoretic closure; Stacks Tag 03GI, schemes.tex, lemma-quasi-compact-permanence.

proof.text: Apply [def-nagata-dense-refinement] and [prop-nagata-dense-refinement] to $c_0$. They give a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of the same morphism $f$ with ambient scheme $\overline X=\operatorname{SIm}(j_0)$. Since $j_0$ is a quasi-compact immersion by step 1, [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] identifies its factor $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ as a quasi-compact open immersion with topologically dense image. This proves the compactification and density assertions for the specified construction, rather than choosing a different compactification.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: "replace the compactifying scheme by the scheme-theoretic closure of X".

proof.text: The scheme $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$. Indeed $p$ is proper, hence finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $Y$ is finite type over $k$. In the affine-cover definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], refine a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $Y$ by the finite affine covers $\operatorname{Spec}C_{it}$ of their inverse images under $p$. Each $B_i$ has finitely many $k$-algebra generators and each $C_{it}$ has finitely many $B_i$-algebra generators; their combined lists generate $C_{it}$ over $k$. There are finitely many such affine charts, proving the assertion.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: finite type of the refined compactifying scheme; affine-generator expansion of composition of finite-type morphisms.

proof.text: Apply the dense-open clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] to $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$. Its ambient scheme is finite type over the field $k$ by step 3 and its image is dense by step 2. Therefore $\dim\overline X=\dim X\leq d$. In particular the dimension bound is obtained from the dense refinement and does not require the original $\overline X_0$ to have dimension at most $d$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: "Its dimension is at most d"; dense-open dimension equality (Stacks Tag 0A21, varieties.tex, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic).

proof.text: Fix any $n\geq1$ and any input $L$ as in the statement. Apply [lem-trf-open-ctf] to $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $A=A_n$. Both schemes are finite type over $k$. The hypotheses give intrinsic bounded constructibility and Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $L$, so the lemma gives $j_!L\in D^b_{ctf}(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ with exactly the same Tor interval. Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] to $p:\overline X\to Y$ and $j_!L$. Properness of $p$ gives separatedness and finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and step 4 supplies $\dim\overline X\leq d$. The corollary applies to the intrinsic pro-étale categories and returns intrinsic bounded constructibility and Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$ for $Rp_{*,n}j_!L$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: extension by zero preserves constructibility and Tor interval; apply the finite direct-image Tor bound, using its intrinsic pro-étale corollary.

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) on $L$: it supplies a bounded constructible étale complex and an étale-origin isomorphism for $L$. Thus $L$ belongs to the precise domain of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]. Apply that proposition to $c$ and the originally fixed $c_0$. Its canonical compactification comparison gives $\alpha:Rp_{*,n}j_!L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}L=F_nL$. All its scheme hypotheses hold for the given $X,Y,f$, and $\ell$ is invertible in the characteristic-$p$ field $k$ because $\ell\ne p$. This comparison uses the originally prescribed functor $F_n$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: finite compact-support site comparison, followed by canonical compactification independence; Stacks Tags 09AK and 09AL, proetale.tex, lemma-compare-constructible and lemma-compare-constructible-derived, for the witness domain.

proof.text: For the isomorphism $\alpha$ of step 6, each cohomology sheaf is isomorphic on the two sides. A finite constructible stratification for the left side therefore also witnesses constructibility on the right, and the same finite cohomological support interval works [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For every degree-zero $A_n$-module sheaf $M$, applying the derived tensor functor to $\alpha$ gives an isomorphism $(Rp_{*,n}j_!L)\otimes^L_{A_n}M\cong F_nL\otimes^L_{A_n}M$. Taking cohomology proves the same vanishing outside $[a,b+2d]$ on the right, which is exactly [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The construction of $c$ did not involve $n$, and the two finite-level estimates use the same dimension bound $d$ for every $n$. Since $c_0$ was arbitrary, the numerical interval is independent of both $n$ and $c_0$.
